correctness.rationale: The projection satisfies the Reynolds identity at weight −1 in every characteristic, and the defining relation reduces to QεQ=0. The ideal of the free algebra is spanned exactly by words containing εε or QεQ. An admissible word is a power of Q, has one ε at an end, or has the form εQ^mε with m≥1. In [Q,−], one-ε words of length ≥2 give separate surviving words Q^(a+1)ε and −εQ^(a+1); ε itself gives Qε−εQ. The distinct words cannot cancel, in characteristic 2 either. Then commuting with ε removes all nonconstant Q powers, and every εQ^mε is annihilated on either side by both generators. The resulting central ideal has an infinite strictly increasing chain of finite-dimensional subideals. This argument is independent of the bounded supplied checker, which was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Put Q=(1⊗1)t. In positive degree the theorem gives [Q,−] zero on 1⊗1 and ε⊗ε, with independent images +1⊗ε and −ε⊗1 on the other two basis elements (up to the ordering of those input elements). The two natural R-actions then give [ε,1⊗1]=ε⊗1−1⊗ε, and [ε,ε⊗ε]=0. In degree zero [Q,ε]≠0. The surviving ε⊗ε in each positive degree corresponds to εQ^mε; its products all vanish by P(ε)=P(ε²)=ε²=0.
